summary: Probenecid is a uricosuric drug that inhibits renal tubular reabsorption of uric acid, increasing its excretion to lower serum urate in chronic gout and hyperuricemia. By blocking renal tubular secretion of organic acids, it also prolongs and raises plasma levels of penicillins and cephalosporins, and is used as an antibiotic adjuvant. Adequate hydration and urine alkalinization reduce the risk of urate stones during initiation.
indications: Treatment of hyperuricemia associated with chronic gout and gouty arthritis (not for acute attacks)
Adjunct to penicillin or cephalosporin therapy to elevate and prolong antibiotic plasma concentrations

dosage.d: 250 mg twice daily for 1 week, then 500 mg twice daily
dosage.n: May increase by 500 mg every 4 weeks to max 2 g/day, guided by urate

dosage.d: 1 g as a single dose with the antibiotic
Initial 25 mg/kg, then 40 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses

admin: Take with food, milk or an antacid to reduce stomach upset
Maintain a high fluid intake (about 2-3 L/day) to prevent urate stone formation
Alkalinize the urine (e.g., sodium bicarbonate or potassium citrate) early in therapy as directed
Do not start during an acute gout attack; begin after the attack settles
moa: Probenecid competitively inhibits the renal tubular organic anion transporters that reabsorb filtered uric acid, increasing urinary uric acid excretion and lowering serum urate. The same inhibition of tubular secretion of organic acids reduces renal clearance of penicillins, cephalosporins and other organic-acid drugs, raising and prolonging their plasma concentrations.

absolute: Acute gout attack (do not start therapy during an attack)
relative: Significant renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min - generally ineffective)

preg: Probenecid crosses the placenta. Human data are limited; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: Limited information on excretion into breast milk. Use with caution during breastfeeding.
renal: Uricosuric effect depends on glomerular filtration and tubular secretion; probenecid is generally ineffective when creatinine clearance is below about 30 mL/min and should be avoided in severe renal impairment. Stone risk is highest early - ensure hydration and urine alkalinization.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; monitor for adverse effects.

major: Penicillins/cephalosporins - markedly increased and prolonged levels (intended when used as adjuvant)
Methotrexate - reduced renal clearance and increased toxicity
Ketorolac - reduced clearance; concomitant use contraindicated per labeling
moderate: Antivirals (e.g., aciclovir, ganciclovir, zidovudine) - increased levels
interactions.food: Take with food/antacid to limit GI upset; maintain high fluid intake.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol - it raises serum urate and may provoke gout flares.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum uric acid; may cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests; can interfere with urinary 17-ketosteroid and PSP excretion tests.

serious: Uric acid renal stones / acute uric acid nephropathy

monitoring: Serum urate, aiming for target level; periodic renal function
Adequate hydration and urine pH during initiation
counsel: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to protect your kidneys
Do not take aspirin or aspirin-containing products - they block this medicine's effect
Gout flares may occur when starting - keep taking probenecid and treat the flare as directed
Take with food or an antacid if it upsets your stomach
Tell your doctor if you develop a rash, fever or unusual bruising
pk: Uricosuric effect begins within hours; antibiotic-sparing effect prompt
Plasma peak about 2-4 hours after an oral dose
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: Not for acute gout - it can prolong or worsen an acute attack; start only after the flare settles and use flare prophylaxis
Loses efficacy as renal function declines (CrCl <30 mL/min); switch to xanthine oxidase inhibitor
Classic adjuvant to extend penicillin/cephalosporin levels by blocking tubular secretion
Aspirin/salicylates antagonize the uricosuric action - avoid them
Hydration plus urine alkalinization prevents uric acid stones during initiation
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and continue the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause CNS stimulation, seizures, respiratory failure and cardiovascular collapse. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive with airway protection, seizure control and standard overdose measures. Probenecid is dialyzable.
